text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- EU jobs pact injects a "a bit of social flavour" to Europe's economic agenda, says Le Figaro -- is a "timid relaunch" of Europe's social priorities, according to Les Echos.
But "the euro emerges intact" from the Amsterdam summit, La Tribune says in its page one headline.
Other stories --
LES ECHOS
-- Results of an audit of public finances to be known by mid-July, a summer mini-budget now looks less probable.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Axa-UAP reshuffles organisation in France -- renamed Axa-France will manage operations for its insurers, brokers and staff insurance networks.
-- A new, more restrictive price policy is expected to trigger restructuring in the private clinic sector.
-- Investigators into bankruptcy of Comipar and Pallas Stern question the approval of accounts by audit firms, which may have contributed to a five to eight billion francs hole in accounts.
L'AGEFI
-- Societe Generale may spin off its market activities to subsidiaries, consulting firm studies impact.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Multimedia firm Grolier in talks with France Telecom towards possible co-operation.
-- Japanese cosmetics group Shisheido considers setting up a second plant in France, aims for a ten-billion-franc turnover in its international activities through the year 2000.
LIBERATION
-- Unions call for a hike in the SMIC legal minimum wage, to be re-valued on July 1.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Airbus partners say U.S. aid to Boeing violates a 1992 agreement on subsidies.
